newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end higher following stocks' plunge.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end higher following stocks' plunge.

text.p: *Japanese government bond futures end higher in dealer-led trade following Tokyo stocks' sharp fall. *Remarks by BOJ governor, prime minister and finance minister had little impact, traders said. *Players cautious about possibility of further yen weakness.
Matsushita, speaking to a meeting of BOJ branch managers, said Japan's economy was continuing its gradual recovery and the strength of this recovery was gradually increasing.
"People were a bit jittery ahead of Matsushita's speech, but his remarks had little impact as it did not contain anything fresh," said the brokerage house trader.
Matsushita also said that the central bank was keeping close watch on the impact on the economy of falls in Japanese share prices.
Hashimoto and Mitsuzuka's speeches at the opening of parliament were also virtually ignored by the bond market.
Hashimoto said the government would seek early enactment and smooth implementation of the supplementary budget and fiscal 1997 budget.
Mitsuzuka said Japan's economy was continuing to recover at a gradual pace, with private-sector demand increasing in firmness.
Bond traders see a possibility of the key March contract testing 126.58 in the near future, an all-time high for any benchmark contract set on November 28, 1996.
However, some were cautious about the risks of further yen weakness.
The dollar rose as high as 117.90 yen in Tokyo trade.
"The yen's weakness was one of the reasons people in the JGB market were cautious about testing higher levels," said a a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is planning to hold an auction for 20-year JGBs on Tuesday, a MOF official said.
Traders said the offer was likely to be about 400 billion to 500 billion yen with the coupon rate set at around 3.3 percent.
